capturedAt: 2026-09-09 15:43 MYT · Sep 8 US closes + Sep 9 dossier + MacroMicro cross-market validation
title: Power Stack Watchlist
method: Action-oriented queue combining business quality, plausible upside, downside/funding risk, valuation, technical location, current theme significance and portfolio overlap. Structural quality and buy-now quality remain separate. MacroMicro is used as a supporting cross-market verification layer; fresher official data controls when available.
marketRegime: Inflationary physical-capex expansion confronting a global duration shortage. US10Y 4.79%, real10Y 2.42%, Japan10Y 2.89%, tight broad IG spreads but 10.55% CCC OAS, near-$100 oil and peak-load stress favour existing generation, regulated grid, funded backlog, refiners/logistics and strategic hedges over financing-dependent duration.

buckets.label: Buy / Accumulate
buckets.description: Price, business quality and current theme setup are aligned enough for staged entry.

buckets.label: Selective / Retest
buckets.description: Good business/theme, but current price, tactical macro risk or overlap requires a better level or confirmation.

buckets.label: Wait / Confirm
buckets.description: Interesting exposure, but current risk/reward or cyclical timing is not strong enough to force.

buckets.label: Avoid / High Risk
buckets.description: Financing, valuation, dilution or execution risk currently dominates.

candidates.name: Cameco
candidates.thesis: Still the best blend of strategic scarcity, real operating economics and limited dependence on project-finance duration. The new duration regime strengthens the preference for fuel-cycle assets over pre-revenue reactor concepts.

candidates.name: Vistra
candidates.action: TOP-TIER RETEST WATCH / DO NOT CHASE
candidates.theme: Existing generation · CAISO peak load · AI power scarcity
candidates.thesis: Existing dispatchable generation, signed PPAs and funded counterparties are exactly what the duration-shortage regime rewards. CAISO heat turns the power thesis into operating evidence. Stronger thesis, worse chase risk.

candidates.name: Tenaga Nasional
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <RM13.00 or weakening regulated grid/DC economics
candidates.theme: Malaysia grid · regulated power · data-centre load
candidates.thesis: Malaysia data-centre demand is now observed load rather than forecast demand. Regulated transmission/distribution gives a lower-duration way to own the buildout than speculative project developers.

candidates.name: Valmont Industries
candidates.thesis: Attractive crossover between grid hardening, water efficiency and climate/heat adaptation, with better current entry asymmetry than stretched mega-cap electrical names.

candidates.name: Eaton
candidates.thesis: Peak-load and real interconnection demand strengthen the business, but price is already beyond the old entry zone. MacroMicro's duration data argue against chasing premium valuation.

candidates.name: Quanta Services
candidates.thesis: Actual awarded work and record backlog make PWR one of the cleanest funded-demand beneficiaries. Buy-now asymmetry is weaker after the breakout.

candidates.name: MN Holdings
candidates.thesis: Strong FY26 growth and ~RM1.64bn order book give company-specific proof behind the Malaysia grid thesis. Price is near highs, so research priority rises faster than buy-now attractiveness.

candidates.name: SPDR Gold MiniShares
candidates.entry: Stage on stabilisation or real-yield pullback rather than headline spikes
candidates.confirmation: Gold holds/reclaims trend while real yields stop rising
candidates.invalidation: Persistent real-yield/USD breakout with major gold support loss
candidates.thesis: Promoted from lower-tier hedge to strategic allocation candidate. China reserve buying and global duration stress strengthen the structural case, but MacroMicro real10Y at 2.42% keeps tactical timing important.

candidates.name: Cheniere Energy
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$268 or rapid normalisation of LNG security economics
candidates.thesis: Saudi/Hormuz escalation and Japan/Asian energy-security concerns raise the value of non-Hormuz contracted LNG capacity.

candidates.name: CF Industries
candidates.thesis: Energy and shipping stress strengthen nitrogen economics, but diesel/fertilizer inflation also squeezes farmer affordability. Strong thesis, poorer entry after rally.

candidates.name: Valero Energy
candidates.entry: No chase after seven straight gains; wait for first orderly pullback
candidates.confirmation: Product cracks remain extreme with high refinery utilisation
candidates.thesis: New addition. The dossier shifts energy emphasis downstream: diesel/product scarcity can stay strong even if Brent stalls. VLO is the cleanest current momentum expression, but price is extended at fresh highs.

candidates.name: Marathon Petroleum
candidates.entry: No chase after nine straight gains; wait for pullback or crack reset
candidates.confirmation: Persistent diesel/gasoline cracks and throughput economics
candidates.invalidation: Rapid product-inventory rebuild or crack collapse
candidates.thesis: New addition. Strong direct beneficiary of the refined-products regime, but almost exactly at its 52-week high.

candidates.name: Phillips 66
candidates.entry: Wait for pullback; current price is within ~1% of 52-week high
candidates.thesis: New addition. Useful downstream diversification, but current price already discounts much of the near-term squeeze.

candidates.name: Flex
candidates.confirmation: Named funded backlog + strong cash conversion
candidates.thesis: Physical demand stays strong, but the AI-debt regime raises the premium on signed/funded customers and cash conversion.

candidates.name: Corteva
candidates.thesis: High-quality agriculture exposure remains preferable to machinery while energy/fertilizer costs pressure farm budgets.

candidates.name: NCR Voyix
candidates.thesis: Still attractive asymmetry, but high duration/credit competition raises the penalty for leverage and slow top-line growth.

candidates.name: Bunge Global
candidates.thesis: Food-flow/logistics exposure remains useful in an energy/shipping shock, but current entry is less attractive after breakout.

candidates.name: SLB
candidates.entry: Refresh price; buy only on a post-headline retest
candidates.confirmation: Kelvion integration + cooling growth + stable FCF
candidates.thesis: Unusual dual exposure: Gulf escalation supports services while Kelvion adds cooling. More interesting now, but integration proof remains necessary.

candidates.name: Freeport-McMoRan
candidates.price: Fresh quote required after Sep 8 surge
candidates.invalidation: Inventory rebuild and weaker grid/China demand
candidates.thesis: Record copper validates scarcity, but MacroMicro China credit data argue against treating the move as broad China reflation. Stronger thesis, tighter entry discipline.

candidates.name: CrowdStrike
candidates.thesis: Mission-critical software survives, but a 4.79% US10Y and S&P earnings yield below Treasury yield make premium duration less attractive relative to physical scarcity.

candidates.name: Agnico Eagle Mines
candidates.action: QUALITY GOLD / WAIT FOR REAL-YIELD STABILISATION
candidates.confirmation: Gold trend stabilises with real yields easing
candidates.invalidation: AISC/production deterioration or gold support loss
candidates.thesis: Moves higher with the strategic gold theme, but GLDM remains the cleaner first implementation under high real yields.

candidates.name: Nutrien
candidates.thesis: Benefits from input scarcity but is more exposed than CF to farm-affordability and potash deferral risk.

candidates.name: Wheaton Precious Metals
candidates.confirmation: Gold holds with easing real yields
candidates.thesis: Cleaner cost structure than miners; still below GLDM/AEM for current implementation.

candidates.name: Salesforce
candidates.entry: Only after valuation reset and stabilisation
candidates.invalidation: AI monetisation or FCF momentum fades
candidates.thesis: High-quality but on the wrong side of the duration regime; software-specific AI competition adds another reason not to force entry.

candidates.name: FirstCash Holdings
candidates.confirmation: Double-digit pawn receivable growth with FCF intact
candidates.invalidation: Receivable growth normalises or leverage/regulation worsens
candidates.thesis: The consumer is not collapsing, but high fuel and finance costs strengthen the late-cycle trade-down thesis.

candidates.name: Coinbase Global
candidates.confirmation: Activity/USDC/FCF remain strong with lower real yields
candidates.thesis: Good company-specific fundamentals, but global duration and weak-end credit make liquidity beta relatively unattractive.

candidates.name: Bitcoin
candidates.entry: Only on disciplined pullback and improving liquidity
candidates.confirmation: Improving flows with easing real yields
candidates.thesis: Structural scarcity remains, but physical cash-flow scarcity and gold now rank better in the current cross-asset regime.

candidates.name: Symbotic
candidates.thesis: Commercial automation remains valid, but funding/customer-capex sensitivity lowers relative priority.

candidates.name: Strategy
candidates.entry: No entry until credit/liquidity regime improves
candidates.confirmation: BTC strength with financing stress easing
candidates.thesis: The global duration shortage directly worsens the mechanics of leveraged crypto convexity.

candidates.name: NuScale Power
candidates.entry: No entry until funded project and customer backstop exist
candidates.thesis: Nuclear is strategically strong, but pre-revenue project finance sits on the wrong side of the duration shortage. Prefer CCJ/BWXT/CW/VST instead.

priceCoverageNote: Fresh Sep 8 closes are used where verified. Several lower-priority names retain prior references or require a fresh quote before action. Theme promotion never overrides entry discipline.
